title: Why Is My Dryer Drum Not Turning?

seo.title: Why Is My Dryer Drum Not Turning?
seo.meta_description: If the dryer powers on but the drum will not turn, separate overload, obstruction, belt, and motor clues before attempting a repair.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a dryer drum that will not turn and know which external checks are safe before service.

excerpt: If the dryer appears to start but the drum stays still, listen closely. Silence, humming, and an unusually free-spinning drum point in different directions.
content_html:
When the dryer powers up but the drum stays still, the sound matters. A hum, a click followed by silence, and a drum that suddenly turns very freely by hand suggest different failure paths.

Rule out an overloaded drum

Turn the dryer off, remove part of the load, and try a small load. Wet comforters, rugs, and other heavy items can require much more starting torque than ordinary clothing.

Look for an obvious obstruction with power off

A garment, drawstring, or small object can wedge near the drum edge. Inspect only areas reachable from the door; do not probe behind panels.

Hand rotation is a clue, not a diagnosis

With the dryer unplugged, many drums have some smooth resistance. If yours suddenly feels much easier to turn than it used to, a broken drive belt is possible. If it is unusually hard to move, a roller, idler, or trapped object may be binding.

A humming motor should not be repeatedly stalled

If a light load does not change the symptom, stop cycling Start over and over. A stalled motor can overheat.

Most drive repairs require cabinet access

The belt, idler pulley, rollers, and motor are internal parts. Disconnect the dryer if you smell hot insulation, see sparks, or the breaker trips. Do not let a dryer continue heating while the drum is stationary because the load cannot tumble and distribute heat normally.

Before scheduling service, note whether you can hear the motor, how the unplugged drum feels when turned, and whether the failure happened suddenly. Those observations are more useful than simply reporting “it does not spin.”

faq.question: Can I run the dryer if it heats but does not tumble?
faq.answer: No. A stationary load can overheat because it is not moving through the airflow normally.

faq.question: Does a very loose-feeling drum prove the belt broke?
faq.answer: No, but it is a useful clue. Internal inspection is needed to confirm the drive failure.

faq.question: Should I keep pressing Start if the motor hums?
faq.answer: No. Repeatedly stalling a motor can overheat it.
